title: Scale using training data
summary: Scaling puts features on a chosen numeric scale. Fit the scaler on training data, then use that fitted scaler on other data.
introduction: Scaling puts features on a chosen numeric scale. Fit the scaler on training data, then use that fitted scaler on other data. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: Scaling puts features on a chosen numeric scale. Fit the scaler on training data, then use that fitted scaler on other data.

blocks.code:
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
scaler = StandardScaler()
scaled = scaler.fit_transform([[1.0], [2.0], [3.0]])
print(round(float(scaled[1, 0]), 6))
blocks.title: Scale using training data

blocks.text: The middle value becomes 0.0 because it equals the training mean. Other values are measured relative to the learned spread.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Explain why the test set should not set the training mean.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Fitting the scaler on all data before splitting leaks test information.
